study_name: Meno-J Theory Study 2: Historical J-Jump Calibration Casebook

method.mode: primary-source-led historical stress test with explicit false-jump controls
method.qualification: The case calibrates an engineering contract; it does not settle all historiographical disputes or prove that future AI systems can originate scientific revolutions.

sources.authors: Claudius Ptolemy; George of Trebizond (Latin translator)
sources.title: Almagest manuscript and text record
supports: Ptolemaic combinations of circular motions were explicit geometrical constructions, not a modern caricature.

sources.authors: Johannes Kepler; Bavarian Academy of Sciences edition project
sources.title: The Planetary Laws
supports: The first two laws appear in Astronomia Nova and the third in Harmonice Mundi.
Kepler tied the ellipse claim to physical principles and observations.

sources.title: Front Matter to the Principia, third edition
supports: Newton explicitly connected terrestrial gravity, celestial effects, comet phenomena, and rules of reasoning.

sources.authors: Isaac Newton; I. Bernard Cohen and Anne Whitman (translators)
sources.title: The Principia: Mathematical Principles of Natural Philosophy
supports: Book I develops mathematical consequences of forces; Book III applies them to the system of the world.

sources.authors: José Díez, Gonzalo Recio, and Christián C. Carman
sources.title: Does Explaining Past Success Require (Enough) Retention? The Case of Ptolemaic Astronomy
supports: Ptolemy's Mars model had genuine and risky empirical successes.
Kepler can explain Ptolemy's success without clearly retaining enough of Ptolemy's theoretical machinery.

sources.title: Kepler's Astronomia Nova and the Orbit of Mars
supports: Kepler used a successful vicarious model, pursued physical causes, and treated the eight-arcminute mismatch as evidence against circularity.
The area rule and ellipse emerged through a longer sequence than the simplified textbook story.

sources.title: Kepler and Newton
supports: Kepler's physical astronomy was only partially transmitted to Newton and involved conceptual and computational difficulties.

sources.title: Newton's Philosophiae Naturalis Principia Mathematica
supports: Newton treated Keplerian phenomena as approximate rather than exact.
Universal gravity explained ideal Keplerian motion and departures caused by mutual interactions.
Book III was a sustained evidential argument with major unresolved loose ends.

sources.title: Kepler's Laws of Planetary Motion, Before and After Newton's Principia
supports: Newton transformed the scientific meaning and problem role of the Keplerian laws rather than merely repeating them.

sources.title: O Male Factum: Rectilinearity and Kepler's Discovery of the Ellipse
supports: Kepler's route to the ellipse depended on the interplay of geometry, the area relation, and an attempted physical account.

sources.title: Kepler's Area Law in the Principia: Filling in Details in Newton's Proof of Proposition 1
supports: Newton's Proposition 1 generalized the area law through a central-force framework, although details of the limiting proof have been debated.

historical_models.name: Ptolemaic planetary astronomy
historical_models.representation: Earth-referenced deferent, epicycle, eccentric, and equant constructions for nonuniform apparent planetary motion.
historical_models.strongest_success: It organized retrograde motion and planetary longitudes and produced risky consequences such as Mars brightening near opposition.
historical_models.important_limit: Its successful geometry did not supply the later Sun-centered dynamical relation, and its distances and physical interpretation remained problematic.

historical_models.name: Keplerian physical astronomy
historical_models.representation: Sun-focused ellipses, an area-time relation, and a cross-planet period-distance relation, developed alongside attempted solar physical causes.
historical_models.strongest_success: It replaced circle-based kinematics with laws that jointly described orbital shape and nonuniform motion and exposed precise observational discrepancies.
historical_models.important_limit: Kepler's proposed magnetic/animating physical machinery was not retained as the cause of orbital motion, and the laws were not yet Newtonian dynamics.

historical_models.name: Newtonian celestial dynamics
historical_models.representation: Laws of motion and mutual inverse-square gravitation applied to terrestrial bodies, planets, satellites, tides, Earth shape, and comets.
historical_models.strongest_success: It recovered Kepler-like motion under ideal conditions while explaining deviations through interactions and extending one framework across previously separate phenomena.
historical_models.important_limit: Book III contained approximations, empirical uncertainties, unresolved lunar and planetary details, and no accepted micro-mechanism for gravity.

J1_representation_change.reason: Earth-referenced circle combinations were replaced by Sun-focused ellipses plus an area-time relation.

J2_retention.reason: Kepler recovered and improved empirical successes, but enough Ptolemaic theoretical structure is not clearly retained; some identical numerical roles belong to different objects.

J3_new_reach.reason: The new representation addressed orbital shape, distances, nonuniform speed, and physically meaningful solar organization rather than longitude calculation alone.

J4_compression_control.reason: Geometrical devices were reduced at the representational level, but computation remained difficult and the attempted magnetic mechanism added unsupported structure.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Distance, latitude, and the eight-arcminute octant discrepancy separated the circle-based and elliptical accounts; geoheliocentric and alternative motion rules remained serious rivals.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: The ellipse and area relation exposed exact quantitative consequences that could fail at many orbital positions.

transitions.why_amended_verdict_is_not_whole_theory_: The ellipse/area representation survives; Kepler's causal submodule does not. The transition can be explanatory progress without every accompanying belief being correct.

J1_representation_change.reason: Orbital regularities became consequences and approximations within laws of motion and mutual gravitation centered on the system's center of mass.

J2_retention.reason: Kepler-like ellipses and area behavior are recovered under idealized conditions, while gravitational interactions explain why actual motion departs from the ideal.

J3_new_reach.reason: The framework joined terrestrial and celestial gravity and addressed satellites, perturbations, Earth shape, tides, precession, and comet trajectories.

J4_compression_control.reason: A smaller common dynamical principle set replaced separate kinematic rules, although derivations and calculations became substantially harder.

J5_rival_discrimination.reason: Earth-shape, latitude-gravity, comet, lunar, and perturbation consequences confronted vortex and alternative force accounts, though several tests remained unresolved for decades.

J6_falsifiability_growth.reason: The theory risked failure across distinct systems and on deviations, not merely on the observations used to state Kepler's laws.

transitions.why_amended_verdict_is_not_whole_theory_: Newton's dynamical relation and unification survive this case; exact historical calculations, all perturbations, and a micro-mechanism of gravity do not receive blanket approval.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.candidate: Add another epicycle without changing the representation family
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.temptation: Accuracy improves, so call it a conceptual jump.
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: Potentially good science and improved prediction, but J1 fails unless variables, relations, levels, or contrasts genuinely change.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.candidate: Exact lookup table for all Tycho observations
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: No warranted bridge, no transport to changed cases, no rival discrimination, and no new risky consequence.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.candidate: Kepler's magnetic or animating mechanism taken by itself
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.temptation: It introduced physical causation into mathematical astronomy.
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: Novelty and falsifiability do not compensate for a failed causal warrant. Its failure does not erase the orbital representation component.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.temptation: Either call it the complete revolution or dismiss it because initial positional accuracy did not improve.
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: It reorganized planetary order and retrograde relations, but retained circular devices and does not receive the later Kepler-Newton achievements retrospectively.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.temptation: Dismiss it because heliocentrism later won.
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: Contemporary observational equivalence means the contract must record underdetermination and seek future discriminators rather than rewrite history.

false_jump_and_boundary_controls.candidate: Fit an ellipse with a Fourier or epicycle expansion and call the basis functions retained
false_jump_and_boundary_controls.reason: A shared fit or mathematical translation need not preserve what the variables represent or why the model succeeds.

contract_amendment.trigger: The Ptolemy-to-Kepler transition fails the original literal/special-case reading of J2 even though the orbital representation is a defensible J-jump.

amendments.old_rule: Previously validated consequences are preserved as a special case, or their failure boundary is explicitly demonstrated.
amendments.new_rule: Account for prior success by at least one declared mode: literal component retention; limiting or approximate derivation; empirical-capability recovery; or a non-retentive explanation of why, how well, and where the old account succeeded and failed.
amendments.guardrail: Mathematical transformability or identical fitted values do not count by themselves; represented objects and evidential roles must be mapped.

amendments.old_rule: Promote or reject the proposal as one unit.
amendments.new_rule: Declare the component under evaluation—representation, empirical law, mechanism, ontology, or method—and permit different verdicts for coupled components.
amendments.guardrail: A successful component cannot launder an unsupported mechanism, and a failed mechanism cannot erase an independently warranted representation.

amendments.old_rule: The jump removes assumptions or detail without losing warranted consequences.
amendments.new_rule: Report conceptual, ontological, parameter, and computational complexity separately. A jump may compress principles while increasing derivational or computational work.
amendments.guardrail: Do not treat shorter prose or fewer named objects as evidence of genuine compression.

amendments.old_rule: The new representation preserves prior validated consequences.
amendments.new_rule: Specify whether consequences are exact, approximate, idealized, or historically provisional, and state the interactions or conditions that generate deviations.
amendments.guardrail: Never describe the Newtonian many-body solar system as exactly Keplerian.

amendments.old_rule: List a strongest rival and divergent prediction.
amendments.new_rule: Allow a temporary observational-equivalence verdict. When current evidence cannot discriminate rivals, record the equivalence class and the new observations or concepts needed to separate it.
amendments.guardrail: Later victory cannot be used as evidence that the earlier rival was irrational or already empirically refuted.

revised_survival_rule.candidate_threshold: J1 representation change passes and the claimed component states J2-J6 obligations.
revised_survival_rule.survival_threshold: For the claimed component, G0-G3 and G5 pass; J2 passes by an explicit retention-accounting mode; J3, J5, and J6 pass; J4 may be partial only when each complexity dimension and tradeoff is declared.
revised_survival_rule.verdict_scope: Every verdict names its component, evidence period, approximation status, and unresolved submodules.

results.original_contract_failure: J2 over-required theoretical retention in the Ptolemy-to-Kepler case and lacked component-scoped verdicts.
results.newton_scope: Provisional dynamical-law success with approximations and historical loose ends; no blanket validation of every calculation or a micro-mechanism of gravity.
significant_findings: A genuine J-jump need not retain the superseded theory's objects; it must account for the old success without ad hoc translation.
J-jump verdicts must be component-scoped: Kepler's orbital representation survives while his magnetic mechanism fails.
Conceptual compression and computational simplicity can move in opposite directions.
Newton's gain was not exact repetition of Kepler but an idealized recovery plus an explanation of deviations and wider phenomena.
Observationally equivalent rivals must remain live until a genuine discriminator exists.

next_case.name: Miasma to germ theory
next_case.reason: It tests whether the amended contract handles multicausal public-health change, partial retention of sanitation success, invisible entities, and rivals without forcing the astronomy pattern onto biology.
next_case.stop_condition: If the same amendment rules require another ad hoc exception rather than generalizing, the J-jump contract must be weakened or rejected before any open-problem AI trial.
